_note: The city bundle's pieces (docs/CITY_BUNDLE_IMPLEMENTATION.md): IL.ranch's five cyberpunk packs, bought by the owner 2026-09-27 and licensed to the owner, not the public. This lists which of their prefabs npm run paid (tools/import-city.ts) bakes, by pack and prefab path under the pack's Prefab folder; the baked files go to public/models/paid/city/ (gitignored, served only by the game server) and each piece's measured size comes back into `measured` below, written by the importer. Names only here: no geometry or texture from the packs is ever committed. `version` names the files (<pack>-v<version>.glb) because the server caches /models/ for a day. `sizes` are the texture sizes of the two builds: hi for the medium and high graphics presets, lo for low. `packages` are the Unity Asset Store downloads' file names.
_pieces: pack: [prefab paths under that pack's Prefab folder, without .prefab]. Grouped by the role each plays in the centre (the plan's section 4.4).
_measured: Written by npm run paid (tools/import-city.ts) off the baked pieces, never typed: each piece's size (w, h, d) and the minimum corner of its bounds in its own space (x, y, z), metres, then its triangles. `facing` is the horizontal side a piece shows most by area (px, nx, pz, nz): the way a facade module faces. `plane`: how far behind a piece's front its wall stands (metres), the plane most of its front area is on, so a thick module's frames and cornices stand out of the building and its wall sits on the building's face.
_dress: How the pieces dress the centre (src/game/citydress.ts, docs/CITY_BUNDLE_IMPLEMENTATION.md sections 4.3 to 4.6). All of it is looks: collision stays the city's own boxes, so the city plays the same with or without the bundle, and every place is chosen by a hash of where it is, never the city's random stream. `outset`: how far a facade module's front stands out of its box's face, inside the plan's 0.15 m (rule 1), enough to keep the two from flickering. `families`: the facade family of each of the centre's 3 by 3 blocks by column and row (x then z, north first), placed so no two neighbours match: Kyber's concrete on the corners, High City's brownstone north and south, Cyber City's upper storeys east and west, Glass City's tech round the Spire; Cyber City's shop fronts go along every podium's street floor whatever the family. Each family's `bay` is its modules' width (measured: High 8 m, Kyber 4 m, Cyber 8 m, Glass 8 m); a face takes as many whole bays as round to its length and stretches them to fit. `ground`, `mid` and `top` are the storeys' modules, a row keeping one module so a facade reads as designed; the Sky Lobby's storey keeps its own walls, so its windows stay open. `tiers`: what each graphics preset draws (quality.ts cityDetail): 0 the buildings, the podiums' shop fronts, the roofs' parapets, the Spire's billboards and the skyline; 1 adds the signs, posters, AC units, blade signs, roof gear, antennas and lamps; 2 adds the cables over the streets, the pipes and wires down the walls and the street clutter. `clear`: how far a piece that stands out of a wall keeps from a pad's column and a stair (metres), and `canyon`: a face with another tower closer than this in front is a canyon's, where nothing stands out of the wall (the chimneys and the jumps are there): it wears `flat` panels, Cyber City's plain concrete, 2 triangles each, as do the bays behind a pad's climb. A thick module's wall stands on the building's face (citykit.json plane, measured), its frames and cornices out of it. The heavy ornate modules are for the ground storey, seen close; the storeys above take the lighter ones. `glow`: pieces whose picture is lit (billboards, posters, screens), their texture also their light at this strength. `relief`: the most a facade module stands out of its building, metres: a module's frames, pilasters and cornices in front of its wall (citykit.json plane) are pressed into this depth, so the wall and its windows sit on the building's face and nothing stands further than half a metre past the collision, where a body walks along a promenade or a jump passes a face. `lean`: what the competitive preset (the one for frames) wears instead: its storeys between ground and roof in the lightest module of each family, Kyber's and Glass's flat, and the lighter shop fronts; everything else is the same, so the city reads the same and draws about half the triangles. The vertical wire runs (`chance.wire`) are off: 3,516 triangles each was 260k for a detail.
_budget: The triangles each graphics preset may draw of the bundle on the centre, counted off the measured pieces by tools/checks/citykit.ts, so verify holds them without the bought files. Set a tenth over what the dressing measured (2026-09-28: competitive, the lean modules, 506k; balanced 891k; high 929k). What that costs, measured with tools/bench.ts from 100 m over the Spire in a match of thirty (skroof), two runs each with the bundle and without (?nocitykit), interleaved, on the owner's RX 9070 XT: competitive 8.2 and 6.7 ms against 7.5 and 6.2; balanced 7.9 and 5.9 against 6.8 and 6.6 (within the noise); high 14.2 and 16.1 against 12.9 and 13.0, high drawing the city again for its live shadows and its ambient occlusion. Raise a number only with a bench beside it.
